literal: Even if one sees the hunger of the mother who gave birth, do not do actions that the noble will condemn.
translation: Even if one has to watch one's own mother suffer from hunger, one must not perform deeds that are condemned by the wise and virtuous.
modern: தன்னைப் பெற்ற தாயின் பசியைக் காண நேர்ந்தாலும், சான்றோர்கள் பழிக்கும் தீய செயல்களைச் செய்யக் கூடாது.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute purity of action under any circumstance. Even the most extreme and emotionally compelling situation, such as seeing one's own mother starve, does not justify committing an immoral act. The poet uses the word 'ஈன்றாள்' (she who gave birth) to evoke the deepest sense of duty and love, yet places the standard of 'சான்றோர் பழிக்கும் வினை' (actions condemned by the noble) as an absolute boundary that must never be crossed. Thus, the purity of the means is held to be supreme, surpassing even the duty of saving a parent's life through wrongful deeds.
